questions.prompt: A Raspberry Pi is powered by a power bank. An Arduino on the Pi's USB port sends PWM to a motor driver, and the driver and motors run from a separate 12 V battery. The motors twitch randomly. What is the most likely fault?
options: The PWM frequency is set too low for the driver chip to follow.
The motors need a much larger capacitor on the Pi's USB port.
The Arduino and driver share no common ground.
The Pi's USB cable is too long to carry serial data reliably.
questions.explanation: A signal is a voltage measured against a reference. If the Arduino ground and the driver ground are not joined, the driver sees a floating input. Join the grounds at one point.

questions.prompt: Which task belongs on the microcontroller rather than on the single-board computer?
options: A 200 Hz wheel speed loop with fixed timing.
Building a map from LiDAR scans with SLAM algorithms.
Detecting people in camera frames with a neural network.
Logging all sensor topics to disk for later replay.
questions.explanation: Fixed-period control with little jitter is the job of the real-time tier. The other three need memory, compute or file storage that a Linux computer has.
questions.skillLabel: Choose MCU or SBC for a task

questions.prompt: A 14-byte register burst read over I2C at 400 kHz. Time in microseconds, using 9 clocks per byte and 3 extra bytes (address+W, register, address+R). Ignore START and STOP.
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points

questions.prompt: The MCU sends 20-byte messages at 50 Hz over a 115200 baud 8N1 UART. What fraction of the link is used? Precision 0.001.
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points

questions.prompt: Which block does a TB6612FNG belong to?
options: Sensor, because it measures the motor current.
Compute, because it contains some control logic.
Power, because it supplies the motors with energy.
Driver, because it switches motor current.
questions.explanation: The TB6612FNG is a dual H-bridge motor driver: it turns low-power logic signals into motor current from the battery.

questions.prompt: A robot moves at 0.8 m/s. Its sensor-to-wheel latency is 45 ms. How many centimetres does it move before the wheels react?
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points

questions.prompt: Trace a ROS 2 velocity command to the wheel of a differential-drive robot with a Pi and a microcontroller. Name each stage and the interface between stages.
rubric: Names the chain: ROS 2 node on the SBC, serial link to the MCU, speed loop on the MCU, PWM and direction to the driver, motor power to the gearmotor.
Names an interface on each link (topic, USB or UART serial, PWM plus direction pins, motor power leads).
Says why the speed loop sits on the MCU (real-time timing) and mentions one failure point such as ground or power.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: A robot works on the bench over USB but the Arduino resets whenever both motors start from the battery. What do you check first?
options: Whether the sketch has a bug in the setup() function.
The logic supply voltage when the motors start.
Whether the serial baud rate matches on both ends.
Whether the encoder wires are twisted together neatly.
questions.explanation: A reset at the moment of a big load change is the classic sign of a supply sag or brownout. Measure the logic rail while the motors start.
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points
